subject: Quick time mix-up
text: Hi there, I hope your morning is going well and that the week has not already piled up too much. I meant to send this earlier, but after rereading our notes I realized I had completely misread the calendar entry and thought we were meeting tomorrow afternoon instead of today. That is entirely my fault, and I am sorry for any inconvenience this may have caused, especially because I know your afternoon is often filled with short check-ins, unexpected requests, and the usual last-minute project twists. I certainly did not intend to make your schedule harder or leave you waiting while I was confused, so thank you for being so accommodating with the change. Would it be alright if we moved our conversation to tomorrow at the time I had assumed? If tomorrow still does not work, I can be flexible in the early evening or before the morning standup, and I will make sure to send a new invite as soon as you let me know. I am genuinely grateful for your patience while we untangle this small mix-up. Thank you for understanding, and I hope the rest of your day goes smoothly enough to give you a little breathing room. Warmly, friend
